newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BCP 1996 profit rises 14.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BCP 1996 profit rises 14.8 percent.

text.p: Portugal's biggest private bank Banco Comercial Portugues, benefiting from a surge in loans and insurance business, posted a 14.8 percent hike in 1996 net consolidated profit to 23.268 billion escudos ($140 million).
BCP announced a 1996 dividend of 70 escudos per share, up from 62.1 escudos per share in 1995, which was adjusted for a dilution in the number of shares after a capital increase.
The bank said 1996 results were not fully comparable with 1995 results because of its acquisition of another Portuguese bank, Banco Portugues do Atlantico (BPA), in 1995.

It said in a statement that an increase in business from consumer credit, mortgages and project finance, as well as loans to small and medium sized companies had boosted its results in a climate of falling interest rates.
The bank also said that it had benefited from increased sales of insurance products in its branches.
BCP said synergies from its merger with BPA would have a positive impact on its results soon.
The total number of employees of BCP and BPA fell to 11,415 in 1996 from 12,534 in 1995 as the bank reduced staff via early retirement programmes.
